parallel.requirements: The run recognized the ESM/.mjs requirement, no external modules, manual CLI parsing, required flags --a through --i, construct-like byte builders, byte-string stdout matching, and the unused-but-required --e field.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation, integration, and delivery ownership while delegating advisory work to a CLI probe child and a workspace scan child. No child owned final output files.
parallel.implementation: The parent created a granular module hierarchy for CLI spec/parsing, numeric builders, text builders, Python bytes formatting, app orchestration, and the test19.mjs entry file.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All code was added in one parent patch under /output and then a small parser portability patch was applied; artifact validation later found test19.mjs and all referenced local modules.
parallel.verification: The parent compared visible sample output against the executable, checked help, missing args, invalid ints, duplicate flags, unknown args, range failures, and non-ASCII string length failure behavior.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 3 of 30. The mounted evidence points to an ordinary formatter gap: the generated bytes formatter always wraps output in single quotes even though the executable can choose double quotes for apostrophe bytes.

serial.requirements: The run recognized the same ESM/.mjs, manual CLI, no-dependency, byte-output, construct Int8ul/Int16ul/Bytes, and /output delivery requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent owned all probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery; no delegation or subagent behavior appears in status or ledger evidence.
serial.implementation: The serial run created a smaller module hierarchy with spec, cli, builders, python-bytes, index, and test19.mjs, using BigInt for parsed integers and local ESM exports.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single parent wrote all modules together, then applied two targeted patches to the CLI negative-number heuristic before final delivery.
serial.verification: It ran all four samples, help and required-argument cases, invalid ints, unknown flags, duplicate flags, equals syntax, construct range failures, multibyte string failures, and targeted negative-number retests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 3 of 30. The code evidence shows the same bytes repr quote-selection weakness for apostrophe bytes despite the run having observed such executable output.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial parent likewise wrote the entire submitted tree and applied later parser patches without any concurrent writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no observed shared-state collision in parallel; the larger tree was parent-integrated from the start, while serial used a flatter tree.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had stronger CLI edge verification, but neither run verified the apostrophe bytes repr behavior against its own formatter after observing the executable form, and both failed official hidden tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout in about 254 agent seconds, used high token volume due to children, and delivered before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout in about 276 agent seconds, used no subagents, and delivered before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more aggregate tokens but did not exhaust the run budget or close under a missing deliverable; both closed with artifacts accepted but official solution_passed false.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed at 27 of 30. Parallel's subagents changed process shape by adding advisory probing and workspace inspection, while the parent still authored and submitted the implementation. Serial did more direct late refinement of negative-number CLI parsing. The strongest concrete shared failure class is ordinary implementation behavior around Python bytes repr quote selection for apostrophe bytes or strings: both implementations escaped apostrophes inside single-quoted bytes output even though the executable showed double-quoted bytes repr in those cases. Because the outcome is the same and no child-owned work was lost, overwritten, or unintegrated, this supports no retained parallel coordination pattern.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation covered visible samples and common parser cases but used an always single-quoted bytes formatter.
Two advisory children increased parallel activity but did not own submitted code or create a proven adverse coordination boundary.
serial_contributors: Single-thread implementation covered visible samples and more negative-number parser cases before final delivery.
The serial bytes formatter also used a single-quoted output style for apostrophe bytes, matching the likely shared hidden failure class.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial corrected negative decimal option-value handling after observing a mismatch; parallel did not show that same correction.
Both runs appear to share an ordinary Python bytes repr quote-selection defect, independent of parallel coordination.
evaluator_effects: The mounted official records expose only aggregate 27/30 results, not per-hidden-case failure logs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported shared ordinary implementation defect, not a parallel coordination cause
